description: SeaSentry is an environmental technology team exploring how satellite radar and geospatial data can help detect potential marine oil-spill anomalies. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we aim to build a prototype for “Dancing with the SARs” using NISAR data and interactive mapping. We welcome teammates skilled in Python, AI/ML, SAR remote sensing, GIS, data visualization, and web development.

details:
SeaSentry is a satellite-assisted environmental incident-management platform designed to support the monitoring and assessment of potential oil-spill incidents in the Caspian Sea.

The platform uses Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery to identify suspicious dark-surface patterns that may require further investigation. Its current detection pipeline applies classical, feature-based computer vision techniques to analyze SAR imagery and flag candidate areas for human review. These outputs are preliminary indicators, not automatic confirmation of oil pollution.

Beyond detection, SeaSentry provides an integrated workflow for environmental incident management. Its working MVP includes backend APIs, authentication and role-based access, incident reporting and management, evidence review, human decision recording, response planning, and PDF report generation.

The platform is designed to help maritime and environmental teams organize incident-related information, assess potential threats, document decisions, and coordinate follow-up actions more effectively.

The project combines satellite remote sensing, computer vision, backend software engineering, and environmental problem-solving. Its current prototype includes Python-based image-processing components and a web-based application.

SeaSentry is important because potential oil spills can pose serious risks to marine ecosystems, biodiversity, and coastal communities. By connecting satellite-assisted monitoring with structured incident-management workflows, we aim to support more informed and coordinated environmental responses.

Our long-term vision is to develop a reliable, explainable, and human-centered decision-support platform tailored to the environmental challenges of the Caspian Sea.
